This is a task from an agent benchmark: 'You are given 20 mL of a sample solution which is created by dissolving an unknown, pure inorganic salt in distilled water. The salt consists of one type of cation and one type of anion. Your task is to perform tests and experiments on the sample using the given tools and reagents, and use the resulting observations to deduce the identity of the unknown salt.'

Below are a few scenarios that may contain an agent's correct/incorrect thought-action pairs.

Scenario A: <thought>Based on the observations: a pale-yellow AgBr precipitate formed with AgNO3 and was insoluble in dilute NH3, confirming Br- as the anion. A white precipitate formed with KOH and dissolved in excess strong base, indicating an amphoteric hydroxide.</thought><action>Final Answer: ZnBr2</action>
Scenario B: <thought>The pale-yellow precipitate that formed with AgNO3 and was insoluble in dilute NH3, indicates bromide as the anion. A white precipitate formed with KOH and dissolved in excess strong base, indicating an amphoteric hydroxide.</thought><action>Test the solubility of the white precipitate from KOH in NH3 to distinguish between Zn+2 and Al+3</action>
Scenario C: <thought>A pale-yellow precipitate with AgNO3 that was insoluble in dilute NH3, confirms Br- as the anion. A white precipitate formed with NH3 and did not dissolve in excess NH3.</thought><action>Final Answer: MgBr2</action>

Which scenario corresponds to a correct thought-action pair?
